## Security hardening: residue quarantine containment, hive promotion provenance, and external-skill approval identity

Three guardrail hardenings land together (collated #3820 + #3822 + #3836, Workstream S slots 3/5/18).

### Residue quarantine rollback + render consistency (#3836, transfers #3596)

- `rollbackResidueQuarantine` no longer aborts an entire batch because one manifest entry carries control characters in its recorded path. Such entries are now **skipped and reported** (`status: 'skipped'`, reason `unsafe-name`), the batch is retained (`drained: false`), and every valid sibling still restores. Previously one poisoned entry threw away the whole rollback and stranded the batch permanently — every retry re-selected it and re-threw, making the stored copies unrecoverable through the tool.
- Tampering stays a hard reject: traversal (`..`), empty segments, absolute paths, and root escapes abort the whole call exactly as before (including when only the stored path is traversal-shaped).
- `validateRelPath` now rejects the full Unicode Cc class (C0 + DEL + C1); previously C1 and DEL passed validation and reached raw output.
- All quarantine/residue-derived names rendered by `swarm config doctor`, the close command (operator warnings and the persisted `.swarm/close-summary.md`), close dry-run, close archive, and the curator post-mortem briefing are neutralized through one shared helper (`neutralizeResidueName`), matching the #3542 renderer treatment.
- The quarantine MOVE path validates each eligible entry's name **before** renaming; unsafe-named residue is preserved in place with reason `unsafe-name` instead of being written raw into a manifest that would later poison rollback.

### Hive promotion is bound to independent provenance (#3820)

- The application-evidence gate is **active by default**: `knowledge.promotion_min_terminal_applications` now defaults to **1** (was 0, which left the gate inert). A lesson is no longer promotable to the cross-project hive on age alone, on a caller-supplied tag, or on retrieval-only phase confirmations without at least one independent terminal receipt. Independent terminal receipts of any outcome (applied, violated or contradicted) satisfy the evidence gate, as defined by the existing #1847 contract; applied-only filtering is not part of this change.
- Independence is an explicit allowlist — only `reviewer`, `architect`, and `test_engineer` receipts count. `delegate` self-report, `architect_marker` acknowledgments, application-gate release records, `manual`, `migration`, `phase_override`, and legacy `unknown` sources are all refused.
- The privileged `hive-fast-track` route is no longer armed by the entry's `tags` array (which any writer could set); it requires a dedicated `hive_fast_track_authorized` field that only the manual promotion path writes, and `knowledge_add` strips the tag from caller input as defense in depth.
- **Compatibility:** ordinary direct-text promotion (`/swarm promote "<text>"`) now requires the audited override (`--force --reason`); `promoteFromSwarm` promotes when the swarm entry has a qualifying independent receipt. Operators who need the old behavior can set `promotion_min_terminal_applications: 0` explicitly.

### External-skill approval is bound to verified content (#3822)

- Promoted external skills are now **digest-bound**: promotion records a canonical content digest (the artifact's own digest line — only an exact `content_digest: <64 hex>` line (or the internal `pending` draft token) — replaced by a fixed placeholder before hashing; a digest line carrying any other value or trailing bytes is hashed as-is, so payload hidden on that line fails verification), and the skill propagation gate recomputes it at discovery/injection time, failing closed on any mismatch — including after an attacker rewrites both body and frontmatter digest, substitutes the candidate id, or strips provenance fields (stripped provenance is still c

# Ownerless plan lock recovery

## What

`tryAcquireLock` now recovers an empty or invalid-JSON `.lck` file once it is
past the lock TTL, matching the recovery behavior already shipped for the
evidence and events stores. Previously such a lock wedged every plan writer
(including `/swarm reset`) until a human deleted the file.

## Why

A torn or empty `.lck` artifact (crash mid-write, truncated write, legacy
ownerless artifact) carries no owner pid, so the `dead-owner` breaker class
returned `unknown` and the acquire path never broke it. The only recovery route
was `cleanupExpiredLocks`, which has no production caller. Plan writers that
use `tryAcquireLock` directly (not via a wrapper with its own contention-loop
break) were permanently wedged.

## Migration

No breaking changes. The fix adds a `ttl-cleanup` branch to the contention path
for ownerless payloads; fresh (within-TTL) ownerless locks still time out as
before.
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->

# Scope binding store lifecycle: deny ledger, class-faithful diagnostics, reset recovery, tombstone preservation

## What changed

- `SCOPE_BINDING_STORE_OVERLOADED` is no longer a catch-all: durable-read
  failures that are not capacity (malformed or workspace-mismatched rows,
  import/ledger errors) surface as a new fail-closed
  `SCOPE_BINDING_STORE_UNREADABLE` class with a recovery message that names
  the real store (the `scope-binding` rows of `.swarm/swarm.db`), wired
  through the delegation gate, scope-guard (which also stops falling through
  to the PR-feedback scope when the store is unreadable), the shell write
  path, and the session-wide resolver. A corrupted row can no longer wedge
  every coder write behind a misleading capacity message (#3889).
- A compact per-workspace deny ledger (one coordination row,
  `scope-binding-deny` namespace) now backs immediate terminal-row
  collection: declaration/claim/teardown/compensation/reset transitions
  delete the retired row and install exact-generation deny evidence in the
  same transaction, so stale in-memory authority in another runtime stays
  denied after the row disappears. A transition retires only the row its
  caller named: a different binding stored under the same key and revision
  is refused, and a caller that passes the payload it observed (the reset
  sweep does) retires exactly that content or nothing — legacy rows that
  carry no binding id stay on the key-and-revision check. The legacy `binding-*.json` projection is
  removed with the row instead of being left behind as a tombstone file.
  Time-expired live rows are collected once past the 24h idle-revival window
  (in-window revival candidates are preserved); reads schedule bounded
  maintenance when collectable rows exist. Unbounded superseded/expired
  accumulation is gone (#3889).
- Consequence for expired generations: a lease that lapsed beyond the
  idle-revival window is no longer revived. Until bounded maintenance
  collects its row, a gate that observes it denies the write as
  `SCOPE_BINDING_EXPIRED` (with its expiry); once the row is collected,
  lookups report it as not declared. A generation retired by an
  explicit terminal tombstone is collected at once and resolves as
  not-declared. Both outcomes deny writes and point the architect at
  `declare_scope`.
- Claim/declaration successors commit with admission-pending deny evidence
  in the same transaction (deny-first): a crash or compensation failure can
  never leave an unadmitted live successor authorizable; successful
  admission releases the entry via compare-and-remove.
- `/swarm reset-session` now sweeps the reset sessions' durable scope rows
  (raw-authoritative attribution by owner/parent/workflow session) through
  the same sink and clears the matching in-memory authority. The sweep pages
  past the scan capacity while rows are being removed, and reports honestly
  instead of printing a successful zero. Each line states only what the sweep
  established: a store it could not read (with the rows swept before
  that), a sweep that filled its scan capacity or reached its pass limit
  before it could confirm the store was seen in full, rows no session can
  claim (the realistic corruption, reported as seen), and every row whose
  retirement attempt threw — resolved by the sweep's last listing of it or,
  failing that, read once more before it is reported, so that one still in
  place, one gone or no longer the reset sessions', one found corrupt and
  one the store refuses to read are each reported separately. Because a
  thrown attempt does not say whether the retirement committed, the sweep
  never claims a row could not have been retired; a row gone or handed to
  another session after such an attempt is named in its own line rather
  than dropped, and is not counted as cleared — and the sweep retires only
  the exact content it listed, so a row replaced under the same key and
  revision by diffe

# Persisted-redaction widening: training vault bare-token families, read-compatible versioning, and evidence/forge boundary redaction

## Summary

Two security gaps closed in one delivery. First, the training-content redactor
(`src/training/redact.ts`) gains the bare well-known credential VALUE families
(anthropic, openrouter, openai, github, aws, slack, google, groq, jwt, base64
with the mixed-class guard, azure `AccountKey=`) mirrored from the shell site,
plus the shared JWS scanner (`src/utils/jws-redaction.ts`). The scanner spans
and the bare arms are collected together and MERGED into disjoint ranges, so an
overlapping arm can neither strand a tail nor drop a head. A bare provider
token of one of those families, in prose, no longer reaches the persisted
training vault. The redaction version moves to 2 with a READ-COMPATIBLE
contract: the vault record schema accepts every version 1..2 (pre-v2 records
stay valid, exportable, and — because the expiry sweep now RETAINS
version-only-quarantined lines while purging only expired/malformed/other-invalid
ones — survive rewrites; the physical byte quota is preflight-exact and counts
every retained byte). The consent surface treats `redaction_version` as
informational redactor provenance (the authorization terms are unchanged by a
redactor bump, so older consents stay valid); the export manifest reports the
SOURCE redaction versions represented by the included records SEPARATELY from
the floor every emitted record was verified at, every exported record is
re-redacted by the running redactor (the AT-REST bytes stay as they are until
the user elects migration), and an export that cannot safely redact a record
publishes nothing. Second, the review and forge evidence boundaries gain a
shared superset redactor (`src/security/evidence-redaction.ts`: `redactSecrets`
∪ display bare families ∪ credential-placement shapes ∪ URL-credential
stripping ∪ the shared JWS scanner) applied BEFORE durable writes and outputs:
auto-review evidence, review receipts, the forge event queue (every rewrite
path), the agent wake message, the subscriber advisory construction point, the
PR-feedback loop terminal reasons, the gh-evidence tool result, the published
PR-review submission body, the findings/handoff artifacts (with a salted HMAC
raw-replay identity sidecar preserving exact-replay semantics after redaction),
finding-policy synthesis, and the post-abort partial export.

## Semantics decisions

- Consent compatibility: tolerant-read (v1 consents stay valid under the v2
  redactor and capture continues; provenance semantics documented in the
  consent preview and docs/commands.md). The redaction version is
  informational provenance, NOT a consent-terms boundary — the terms
  (purpose, content classes, quotas, retention, expiry) are the authorization
  surface.
- Export manifest: the SOURCE redaction versions represented by the included
  records are reported separately from the floor every emitted record was
  verified at (the running redactor, because every exported record is
  re-redacted on output). Empty exports carry the running version.
- Already-stored v1 content: document-and-retain with a truthful remediation
  runbook (docs/training-vault-remediation.md: already-stored v1,
  append-triggered sweep with no timer guarantee, exports + copy-outside
  before withdrawal, credential ROTATION as the real remedy, downgrade
  procedure). The EXPORT path re-redacts legacy records on output; the
  at-rest record is never rewritten unless the user opts into migration.

## Safe downgrade (vault)

A downgrade after v2 records exist reinstates the old literal reader and the
old sweep-on-rewrite behavior: v2 records would quarantine `schema_invalid`
and then be physically deleted at the next 256-append sweep. The safe
procedure: **export the vault, copy the export outside plugin control
(withdrawal revokes plugin-side exports with REVOKED.json markers), withdraw
consent, wit

Closes #3770, closes #3773.

- `phase_complete` now REFUSES to complete a phase while any planned task in it is unfinished (status is neither `completed` nor `closed` — the readiness predicate shared with Epic phase-readiness; `blocked` refuses, matching Epic's wave-close semantics). The refusal names the unfinished task IDs (capped at 20, then a count) and returns a structured `update_task_status` recovery. The check runs early (before any state-mutating step, so a refused call leaves `.swarm/` byte-identical and never creates `plan.md`) and again as an always-applicable re-read at the commit boundary — Turbo does NOT bypass it (the turbo enable disclosure now says so). It reads the authoritative plan state observationally (ledger peek with file/SQLite authority resolution; the plan.json projection only when no ledger authority exists), and a ledger authority that exists but cannot be trusted — a torn ledger tail, a resetting crash marker, an unreadable ledger, or duplicate phase ids — REFUSES with `PLANNED_TASKS_UNKNOWN` rather than completing over an unreadable authority. `phase_complete.enabled: false` remains the documented operator bypass of completion enforcement.
- The `phase_complete` core event is now exactly-once (#3770's pinned preserving failure): a normal completion records a durable `phase_completed` ledger event (parity with the close-terminal path; `savePlan` gained `completedPhaseIds`), and the core event is appended through the authority-key dedupe keyed by `(ledger root digest, phase, transition seq)`. Duplicate calls and crash-between-save-and-append retries collapse to one record; a re-rooted plan's new completion gets a distinct identity; concurrent double-calls write one event (the second call returns immediately with the retryable PHASE_COMMIT_LOCKED result before any append — the dedupe additionally guards the sequential duplicate path).
- `getProjectDb` now REFUSES writable open with a typed `schema_newer_than_supported` `ProjectDbError` naming the recorded and supported versions when a database's `schema_migrations` records a newer schema than this client knows (#3773); the global-rules store, the memory sqlite provider, and the memory-family merge destination make the same refusal with an untyped `Error` carrying the same version-bearing message (typed open errors remain scoped to the project `swarm.db`). In every case schema and rows are preserved, `getGlobalDb` closes its raw handle on the refusal, and the `/swarm close` sqlite archive opens its VACUUM INTO source read-only; the read-only diagnostic open (`withProjectDbReadOnly`) is exposed for the project `swarm.db` store, which is also the store whose refusal is typed. Current and supported-older schemas keep opening/migrating exactly as before. Public type surface: `ProjectDbErrorCategory` gains `schema_newer_than_supported` (additive).
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->
